cohort: The cohort consisted of 1405 women whose activity patterns were measured by accelerometers during seven consecutive days in early to mid-pregnancy between 2016 and 2023.
finding: Women with the highest proportion of sedentary behavior had higher adjusted odds of any preeclampsia and a tendency towards higher odds of severe or preterm preeclampsia, while the most physically active women had lower odds of any preeclampsia, with no associations found for other obstetric outcomes.
mod_finding: No associations were found between sedentary behavior or physical activity levels and mode of delivery.
